title: WorstFish vs Zach
summary: Spectator bot-vs-bot game: WorstFish (an engine that plays the worst possible move; white) vs Zach (chess.com 1-Elo bot, 'Martin's nephew'; black). Both bots hang material and avoid captures; Zach ignores mate-in-one chances, under-promotes repeatedly, and the game drags past move 90 with 50-move-rule resets. Ultimately WorstFish loses by forfeit and Zach is declared the winner.
rules: No human player: two bots play each other (WorstFish white, Zach black).
WorstFish: each move, plays the worst legal move by engine evaluation (e.g. 1.g4, 2.f4 inviting mate, Kf2-centre walks).
Zach (1 Elo): random/beginner moves that tend to avoid captures and avoid delivering mate, sometimes under-promotes.
Standard draw rules apply (50-move rule repeatedly nearly triggered).
win_condition: Watch-only. Video outcome: Zach wins by forfeit (WorstFish 'left the game'). For a playable version, player could take Zach's or WorstFish's side (inferred).
